title: APO Halibut with Brown Butter Cauliflower Velouté
description: A lightly toasted butter roux turns cauliflower and milk into a silky white sauce for steamed halibut.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with bottom drip pan, wire rack and food probe
Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: skinless Pacific halibut fillet
ingredients.note: Weight after skin and pin bones are removed. Divide into two even portions about 3/4 to 1 inch thick. Fully thaw before cooking.

ingredients.name: fresh cauliflower florets
ingredients.note: Use the tender tops, chopped small.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted plain meat-and-water broth without a vegetable blend.

ingredients.name: fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves
ingredients.note: Mince the tender leaves to a fine paste.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the APO Gen 1 water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 155°F with sous vide mode on, 100% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 135°F.

steps.title: Soften the cauliflower
steps.text: Simmer {cauliflower} and {broth} in the covered HexClad for 8–10 minutes, until a floret mashes easily.

steps.title: Puree the base
steps.text: Blend the cauliflower and its broth with {milk} until silky. Keep the puree in the heatproof jug and wipe the skillet dry.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Warm {butter} in the HexClad over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, swirling as the milk solids turn golden and smell nutty.

steps.title: Cook the roux
steps.text: Stir {flour} into the browned butter and whisk over low heat for 1 minute.

steps.title: Finish the velouté
steps.text: Whisk the cauliflower puree gradually into the roux, then add {nutmeg}. Simmer for 2–3 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Cover and keep warm.

steps.title: Steam the fish
steps.text: Lay {fish} unbagged in the shallow pan on the middle rack. Insert the probe sideways into the center of the thickest portion. Cook for about 14–28 minutes, checking from 11 minutes or at the probe alert, whichever comes first. Pull each portion at 135°F, verifying both with the instant-read thermometer.

steps.title: Rest under sauce
steps.text: Nestle the fish in the warm cauliflower sauce off heat. Spoon sauce over the top, cover and rest for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Check carryover and doneness
steps.text: After resting, check each thickest center for about 140°F. Open a natural seam with a fork. The center should be opaque and separate easily into flakes. If either cue is unclear or the center is below 140°F, finish covered in hot sauce in the HexClad over low heat to a measured 145°F, checking every minute.

steps.title: Spoon into bowls
steps.text: Set the halibut on a spoonful of velouté in each bowl. Sprinkle {parsley} over the remaining sauce and spoon it generously over both portions.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups for two. Make ahead: Puree the cauliflower and broth up to 2 days ahead. Make the brown butter roux on serving day for the freshest aroma. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the halibut in its velouté for up to 1 month. Stir the sauce gently as it warms to bring the puree back together. Fridge reheat: Place a portion in a covered shallow pan with its sauce. Install the bottom drip pan and set the APO to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the probe target to 165°F and check from 10 minutes until the coldest center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw the covered portion in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge method. For dairy-free velouté, use avocado oil for the roux and plain unsweetened oat milk for the skim milk. Warm the oil briefly before adding flour. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 212 kcal, 30.6 g protein, 8.2 g total carbohydrate, 6.0 g fat, 1.2 g fiber, 153 mg sodium. Includes both the fish and its full share of sauce and any rice or potatoes listed. Sodium varies with the broth.
